data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump claims he 'never cared' about regime change in Iran
data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
Trump claims he 'never cared' about regime change in Iran
US President Donald Trump has claimed that he "never cared too much about the regime" in Iran in an interview with Fox News on Saturday, discussing his strategy to end the current war.
Asked if he expects the Iranian government to outlast the current conflict, Trump said: "Some people said regime change, but you know, explain what that means, because really I've taken out two regimes already."
"You could call that the ultimate regime change," he added.
Trump also said that he was aiming to make a "permanent" deal with Iran that prohibited the Islamic Republic from developing a nuclear weapon.
"I'm going to make it so that if we have an incompetent president in four years or 15 years or 20 years, I'm gonna make a deal that is gonna be permanent. I'm not gonna let somebody allow them to have a nuclear weapon."

data.title: Middle East Eye: 'Will throw keys back to UN': Trump-appointed Board of Peace adviser says Israel blocking efforts
data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
'Will throw keys back to UN': Trump-appointed Board of Peace adviser says Israel blocking efforts
A senior adviser to the US-led Board of Peace for Gaza has said that the panel will "throw the keys back to the UN" if Israel continues to block efforts to prepare for an international stabilisation force and disarm Hamas.
“We have been extremely patient and have given Israel its space,” US official Josh Gruenbaum told the Israeli news site Ynet in an interview published on Friday.
But he said that it was “frustrating” that “Israel is failing to move forward on the commitments Prime Minister Netanyahu made to President Trump”.
“If this political leadership [in Israel] is now telling us that they no longer want to honour what they committed to, then just let us know now - and we’re basically going to throw the keys back to the UN to oversee the mandate,” Gruenbaum said.
Chaired by US President Donald Trump, the Board of Peace was given a sweeping mandate by the UN Security Council in November 2025 to establish an international stabilisation force in Gaza as part of a 20-point plan to end hostilities and rehabilitate the devastated enclave.
While the plan features several Israeli demands, including the full demilitarisation of the Gaza Strip, talks have stalled for months amid disputes over Hamas’ weapons handover and ongoing Israeli attacks, which have killed over 1,600 Palestinians in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire.

The FBI is investigating a breach of its nationwide criminal information database, reported after a series of major technology disruptions in recent weeks.
The intrusion into the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which federal, state and local law enforcement agencies use to share criminal justice information, was discovered in recent days, CNN reported.
The FBI has called it a central law enforcement information system used by agencies across the country. The potential consequences extend beyond the theft of sensitive information.
A former FBI official who led investigations into cybercriminal groups said that officers rely on the database to identify fugitives, check outstanding warrants and access information.
“My concern isn’t simply whether hackers gained access to sensitive information, although that is an issue, but whether they could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on,” the former official told CNN.
FBI director Kash Patel addressed the bureau's cybersecurity efforts on Fox News on Thursday, after officials had learned of the latest intrusion.
Patel touted Operation Winter Shield, an initiative launched earlier this year to encourage companies to strengthen their digital defences and protect sensitive information.
“Other administrations could have made these updates, but they didn’t,” he said.
“We are staying ahead of the curve and making up for lost time.”

data.title: Middle East Eye: Houthi attacks killed 215 children since August, Yemen government says
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Houthi attacks killed 215 children since August, Yemen government says
Houthi attacks on government-held areas killed 215 children between 1 August and 15 November, Yemen’s internationally recognised government said.
Yemen’s ambassador to the United Nations, Abdullah al-Saadi, said the government recorded 3,334 violations against civilians and civilian objects during that period. He said the Human Rights Ministry also documented the deaths of 260 children recruited to fight for the Houthis over three and a half months.
Yemen’s Foreign Ministry said the Houthis exploited schools, pressured families and used summer centres and cultural and religious activities to recruit children.
“These practices constitute grave violations of the rules of international law concerning the protection of children in armed conflict,” the ministry said.
The ministry also recorded 93 attacks on educational facilities and said classes were suspended at 243 schools, affecting 137,000 students.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu's party for Israeli coalition talks
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Eisenkot invites Netanyahu's party for Israeli coalition talks
Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, has invited the right-wing Likud party of caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu for coalition talks, his party said on Saturday.
Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party said the talks, scheduled to begin on Sunday, reflected a "genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government".
Former military chief Eisenkot has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu, after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc.
Saturday's announcement comes as Eisenkot's wide-ranging camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-led lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu's bloc.
"In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow," the party said in a statement.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Hind Rajab Foundation urges Germany to arrest Israeli soldier over Gaza war crimes
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Hind Rajab Foundation urges Germany to arrest Israeli soldier over Gaza war crimes
The Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF) has urged Germany to arrest an Israeli soldier, Almog Keisi, who has been sighted in Luneburg this week, accusing him of war crimes, crimes against humanity and acts of genocide in Gaza.
In a statement, the foundation said it filed a criminal complaint with Germany’s Federal Public Prosecutor in Karlsruhe under the principle of universal jurisdiction set out in Section 1 of the German Code of Crimes against International Law that cover genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes.
German authorities can exercise jurisdiction over these offences regardless of the suspect’s nationality or where the alleged crimes were committed, the statement read.
HRF said that Keisi participated in the burning of residential buildings in Gaza City’s Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood between 9 and 10 October 2025, following the announcement of a ceasefire agreement and ahead of Israeli forces’ withdrawal from northern Gaza.
According to the complaint, Keisi posted photographs on 10 October showing himself placing explosives around civilian objects and later posing in front of buildings engulfed in flames. Other soldiers from the Givati Brigade also shared photographs of the burning structures, describing the destruction as a celebratory farewell.
HRF said it had geolocated the buildings near Al-Mawhobeen Secondary Female School and cited NASA fire-detection data and satellite imagery as corroborating evidence of the fires and damage.
Dyab Abou Jahjah, HRF’s general director, said: “Germany has received evidence against suspected war criminals before and chose to look away. Meanwhile, it arrests and prosecutes people for waving keffiyehs or chanting slogans against the genocide."
"So the question stands: how long will Germany spend its resources prosecuting those who fight the genocide instead of those who commit it?"
